cues.en: Have you ever wondered how it's possible to scratch a CD or a DVD and still have it play back whatever it's storing?
cues.zh: 你有没有想过，CD 或 DVD 被划伤后，为什么还能播放它存储的内容？

cues.en: The scratch really does affect the ones and zeros on the disc, so it reads off different data from what was stored.
cues.zh: 划痕确实会影响光盘上的 0 和 1，所以读出的数据会和原本存储的不一样。

cues.en: But unless it's really scratched up, the bits that it reads off are decoded into precisely the same file that was encoded onto it, a bit for bit copy, despite all of those errors.
cues.zh: 但除非划得很严重，读出的这些比特会被解码成与编码进去时完全相同的文件，一个比特都不差，尽管有那么多错误。

cues.en: There is a whole pile of mathematical cleverness that allows us to store data and just as importantly to transmit data in a way that's resilient to errors.
cues.zh: 有一大堆数学上的巧妙方法，让我们能存储数据，同样重要的是，也能以抗错误的方式传输数据。

cues.en: Well, okay. Actually, it doesn't take that much cleverness to come up with a way to do this. Any file, whether it's a video or sound or text, some code, an image, whatever, is ultimately some sequence of ones and zeros.
cues.zh: 好吧。其实，想出一种办法并不需要多聪明。任何文件，不管是视频、声音、文本、代码、图像还是别的什么，最终都是一串 0 和 1。

cues.en: And a simple strategy to correct any bit that gets flipped would be to store three copies of each bit.
cues.zh: 一个简单的策略是，把每个比特存三份，这样就能纠正任何被翻转的比特。

cues.en: Then the machine reading this file could compare these three copies and always take the best two out of three whenever there's a discrepancy.
cues.zh: 然后读取这个文件的机器可以比较这三份副本，只要出现不一致，就按三份中取多数来定。

cues.en: But what that means is using two thirds of your space for redundancy.
cues.zh: 但这意味着要把三分之二的空间用于冗余。

cues.en: And even then, for all of that space given up, there's no strong guarantee about what happens if more than one bit gets flipped.
cues.zh: 而且就算这样，放弃了这么多空间，也不能有力保证多个比特被翻转时会怎样。

cues.en: The much more interesting question is how to make it so that errors can be corrected while giving up as little space as possible.
cues.zh: 更有意思的问题是，如何做到既能纠正错误，又只牺牲尽可能少的空间。

cues.en: For example, using the method that you'll learn about this video, you could store your data in 256
cues.zh: 比如，用你将在本视频中学到的方法，你可以把数据存储在256

cues.en: bit blocks where each block uses nine bits, nine, to act as a kind of redundancy,
cues.zh: 位块中，每个块使用9位——9位——来充当某种冗余，

cues.en: and the other 247
cues.zh: 其余247

cues.en: bits are free to carry whatever meaningful message or data that you want. And it will still be the case that if any bit gets flipped here, just by looking at this block and nothing more, a machine will be able to identify that there was an error and precisely where it was so that it knows how to correct it. And honestly, that feels like magic.
cues.zh: 位则可以自由携带你想要的任何有意义的消息或数据。而且情况仍然会是：如果这里有任何一位被翻转，仅凭查看这个块、不需要别的信息，机器就能识别出存在错误，并精确地知道错误在哪里，从而知道如何纠正它。说实话，这感觉就像魔法。

cues.en: And for this particular scheme, if two bits get flipped, the machine will at least be able to detect that there were two errors, though it won't know how to fix them. We'll talk a little bit later about how this scales for blocks with different sizes.
cues.zh: 而对于这个特定方案，如果有两位被翻转，机器至少能检测出存在两个错误，尽管它不知道如何修复它们。我们稍后会稍微谈谈，对于不同大小的块，这种方法如何扩展。

cues.en: Methods that let you correct errors like this are known, reasonably enough, as error correction codes.
cues.zh: 能让你像这样纠正错误的方法，被恰如其分地称为纠错码。

cues.en: For the better part of the last century, this field has been a really rich source of surprisingly deep math that gets incorporated into devices we use every day.
cues.zh: 在上个世纪的大部分时间里，这个领域一直是极其丰富的来源，孕育出令人惊讶的深奥数学，并被融入我们每天使用的设备中。

cues.en: The goal here is to give you a very thorough understanding of one of the earliest examples known as a Hamming code.
cues.zh: 这里的目标是让你非常透彻地理解最早的例子之一，即汉明码。

cues.en: And by the way, the way I'm thinking about the structure of this video is less about explaining it as directly as possible and more a matter of prompting you to invent it for yourself with a little gentle guidance here and there. So when you feel like you see where it's going at some point, take that moment to pause, actively predict what the scheme is gonna be before I tell you.
cues.zh: 顺便说一下，我对这个视频结构的考虑，与其说是尽可能直接地解释它，不如说是引导你自己发明它，沿途只给出一点点温和的提示。所以，当你觉得在某个时刻已经看出它要往哪里走时，就趁那个时刻暂停一下，在我告诉你之前，主动预测这个方案会是什么。

cues.en: Also, if you want your understanding to get down to the hardware level, Ben Eater has made a video in conjunction with this one showing you how to actually implement Hamming codes on breadboards,
cues.zh: 另外，如果你想深入理解到硬件层面，Ben Eater 配合这期视频做了一个视频，展示如何在面包板上实际实现汉明码，

cues.en: which is extremely satisfying.
cues.zh: 那感觉极其满足。

cues.en: Now you should know Hamming codes are not as widely used as more modern codes like the Reed Solomon algorithm,
cues.zh: 现在你应该知道，汉明码并不像 Reed Solomon 算法等更现代的编码那样被广泛使用，

cues.en: but there is a certain magic to the contrast between just how impossible this task feels at the start and how utterly reasonable it seems once you learn about Hamming.
cues.zh: 但这项任务在开始时感觉多么不可能，而在你了解汉明码后又显得多么合情合理，这种反差有一种奇妙的魔力。

cues.en: The basic principle of error correction is that in a vast space of all possible messages, only some subset are gonna be considered valid messages.
cues.zh: 纠错的基本原理是，在所有可能消息的巨大空间中，只有一部分子集会被视为有效消息。

cues.en: As an analogy, think about correctly spelled words versus incorrectly spelled words.
cues.zh: 打个比方，想想拼写正确的单词与拼写错误的单词。

cues.en: Whenever a valid message gets altered, the receiver is responsible for correcting what they see back to the nearest valid neighbor, as you might do with a typo.
cues.zh: 每当一个有效消息被改变时，接收方负责将他们看到的内容纠正回最近的有效邻居，就像你可能对拼写错误所做的那样。

cues.en: Coming up with a concrete algorithm to efficiently categorize messages like this, though, takes a certain cleverness.
cues.zh: 不过，要想出一种具体的算法来高效地对消息进行这样的分类，需要一定的聪明才智。

cues.en: The story begins in the nineteen forties when a young Richard Hamming was working for Bell Labs, and some of his work involved using a very big expensive punch card computer that he had only limited access to. And the programs he kept putting through it kept failing because every now and then a bit would get misread.
cues.zh: 故事始于20世纪40年代，当时年轻的 Richard Hamming 在贝尔实验室工作，他的部分工作涉及使用一台非常大且昂贵的打孔卡计算机，而他只能有限地使用它。他不断送入其中的程序总是失败，因为时不时会有一个比特被误读。

cues.en: Frustration being the crucible of invention, he got so fed up that he invented the world's first error correction code.
cues.zh: 挫败感是发明的熔炉，他实在受够了，于是发明了世界上第一个纠错码。

cues.en: There are many different ways to frame Hamming codes, but as a first pass, we're gonna go through it the way that Hamming himself thought about them.
cues.zh: 有很多不同的方式来描述汉明码，但作为初步介绍，我们将按照汉明自己思考它们的方式来探讨。

cues.en: Let's use an example that's simple, but not too simple, a block of 16 bits.
cues.zh: 让我们用一个简单但不至于太简单的例子，一个16位的块。

cues.en: We'll number the positions of these bits from zero up to 15.
cues.zh: 我们将这些位的位置从0编号到15。

cues.en: The actual data that we want to store is only gonna make up 12 of these bits, while four of the positions are gonna be reserved as a kind of redundancy.
cues.zh: 我们实际想要存储的数据只会占据其中的12位，而四个位置将被保留作为一种冗余。

cues.en: The word redundant here doesn't simply mean copy. After all, those four bits don't give us enough room to blindly copy the data.
cues.zh: 这里的“冗余”一词并不是简单的复制。毕竟，那四位并没有给我们足够的空间来盲目复制数据。

cues.en: Instead, they'll need to be a much more nuanced and clever kind of redundancy,
cues.zh: 相反，它们需要是一种更为微妙和巧妙的冗余，

cues.en: not adding any new information,
cues.zh: 不增加任何新信息，

cues.en: but adding resilience.
cues.zh: 而是增加韧性。

cues.en: You might expect these four special bits to come nicely packaged together, maybe at the end or something like that. But as you'll see, having them sit in positions which are powers of two allows for something that's really elegant by the end. It also might give you a little hint about how this scales for larger blocks.
cues.zh: 你可能会期望这四个特殊位整齐地打包在一起，也许在末尾或类似的地方。但正如你将看到的，将它们放在2的幂次位置上，最终会带来非常优雅的效果。这也可能给你一点关于如何针对更大块进行扩展的提示。

cues.en: Also, technically, it ends up being only 11 bits of data. You'll find there's a mild nuance for what goes on at position zero, but don't worry about that for now.
cues.zh: 另外，从技术上讲，最终只有11位数据。你会发现位置0处有一点细微差别，但现在不用担心。

cues.en: Like any error correction algorithm, this will involve two players, a sender who's responsible for setting these four special bits, and then a receiver who's responsible for performing some kind of check and then correcting the errors.
cues.zh: 像任何纠错算法一样，这会涉及两个角色：发送方负责设置这四个特殊位，然后接收方负责执行某种检查，然后纠正错误。

cues.en: Of course, the word sender and receiver really refer to machines or software that's doing all the checks, and the idea of a message is meant really broadly to include things like storage.
cues.zh: 当然，发送方和接收方实际上指的是执行所有检查的机器或软件，而消息这个概念的含义非常广泛，也包括存储之类的事情。

cues.en: After all, storing data is the same thing as sending a message just from the past to the future instead of from one place to another.
cues.zh: 毕竟，存储数据就等同于发送一条消息，只不过是从过去发往未来，而不是从一个地方发往另一个地方。

cues.en: So that's the setup. But before we can dive in, we need to talk about a related idea which was fresh on Hamming's mind in the time of his discovery.
cues.zh: 这就是基本设定。但在深入之前，我们需要讨论一个相关的概念，这个概念在海明发现的那个时代正是他脑海中新鲜的思考。

cues.en: A method which lets you detect any single bit errors but not to correct them, known in the business as a parity check.
cues.zh: 一种方法可以让你检测出任何单个比特错误，但无法纠正它们，业内称之为奇偶校验。

cues.en: For a parity check, we separate out only one single bit that the sender is responsible for tuning, and the rest are free to carry a message.
cues.zh: 对于奇偶校验，我们只分离出一个比特由发送方负责调整，其余比特则自由承载消息。

cues.en: The only job of this special bit is to make sure that the total number of ones in the message is an even number.
cues.zh: 这个特殊比特的唯一职责就是确保消息中1的总数是偶数。

cues.en: So for example, right now, that total number of ones is seven. That's odd. So the sender needs to flip that special bit to be a one, making the count even.
cues.zh: 举个例子，现在1的总数是七，是奇数。所以发送方需要将这个特殊比特翻转为1，使计数变为偶数。

cues.en: But if the block had already started off with an even number of ones, then the special bit would have been kept at a zero.
cues.zh: 但如果这个块一开始就有偶数个1，那么这个特殊比特就会保持为零。

cues.en: This is pretty simple, deceptively simple, but it's an incredibly elegant way to distill the idea of change anywhere in a message to be reflected in a single bit of information.
cues.zh: 这非常简单，简单得有些迷惑人，但它是一种极其优雅的方式，将消息中任何位置的变化浓缩为单个比特的信息。

cues.en: Notice, if any bit of this message gets flipped,
cues.zh: 注意，如果这条消息中的任何比特被翻转，

cues.en: either from zero to one or one to zero, it changes the total count of ones from being even to being odd.
cues.zh: 无论是从0变为1还是从1变为0，都会将1的总数从偶数变为奇数。

cues.en: So if you're the receiver, you look at this message, and you see an odd number of ones, you can know for sure that some error has occurred,
cues.zh: 所以如果你是接收方，看到这条消息，发现1的个数是奇数，你就能确定肯定出错了，

cues.en: even though you might have no idea where it was.
cues.zh: 尽管你可能完全不知道错在哪。

cues.en: In the jargon, whether a group of bits has an even or an odd number of ones is known as its parity.
cues.zh: 用行话说，一组比特中1的个数是偶数还是奇数，称为它的奇偶性。

cues.en: You could also use numbers and say the parity is zero or one, which is typically more helpful once you start doing math with the idea. And this special bit that the sender uses to control the parity is called the parity bit.
cues.zh: 你也可以用数字表示，说奇偶性是0或1，一旦开始用这个思路做数学运算，这样通常更有用。而发送方用来控制奇偶性的这个特殊比特，叫做奇偶校验位。

cues.en: And, actually, we should be clear. If the receiver sees an odd parity, it doesn't necessarily mean there was just one error. There might have been three errors or five or any other odd number, but they can know for sure that it wasn't zero.
cues.zh: 而且，我们得说清楚。如果接收方看到奇数奇偶性，并不一定意味着只发生了一个错误。可能有三处错误、五处或任何奇数个错误，但他们能确定不是零个。

cues.en: On the other hand, if there had been two errors or any even number of errors,
cues.zh: 另一方面，如果出现了两个错误或任何偶数个错误，

cues.en: that final count of ones would still be even.
cues.zh: 最终的1的计数仍然是偶数。

cues.en: So the receiver can't have full confidence that an even count necessarily means the message is error free.
cues.zh: 所以接收方不能完全确信偶数计数就一定意味着消息没有错误。

cues.en: You might complain that a message which gets messed up by only two bit flips is pretty weak, and you would be absolutely right.
cues.zh: 你可能会抱怨，一条消息仅仅因为两个比特翻转就出错，这也太弱了，你说得完全对。

cues.en: Keep in mind, though, there is no method for error detection or correction
cues.zh: 不过要记住，没有任何错误检测或纠正方法

cues.en: that could give you 100% confidence that the message you receive is the one that the sender intended.
cues.zh: 能让你100%确信收到的消息就是发送方想要发送的那条。

cues.en: After all, enough random noise could always change one valid message into another valid message just by pure chance.
cues.zh: 毕竟，足够多的随机噪声总有可能纯靠巧合把一条有效消息变成另一条有效消息。

cues.en: Instead, the goal is to come up with a scheme that's robust up to a certain maximum number of errors or maybe to reduce the probability of a false positive like this.
cues.zh: 而是说，目标是设计出一种方案，能在一定最大错误数范围内保持稳健，或者降低这种误报的概率。

cues.en: Parity checks on their own are pretty weak. But by distilling the idea of change across a full message down to a single bit, what they give us is a powerful building block for more sophisticated schemes.
cues.zh: 单靠奇偶校验本身相当弱。但通过把整条消息的变化概念提炼成单个比特，它们为我们提供了构建更复杂方案的强大积木。

cues.en: For example, as Hamming was searching for a way to identify where an error happened,
cues.zh: 例如，当Hamming在寻找一种方法来定位错误发生的位置时，

cues.en: not just that it happened, his key insight was that if you apply some parity checks not to the full message, but to certain carefully selected subsets,
cues.zh: 而不仅仅是判断是否发生了错误，他的关键洞察是：如果不对整条消息做奇偶校验，而是对某些精心挑选的子集做校验，

cues.en: you can ask a more refined series of questions that pin down the location of any single bit error.
cues.zh: 你就能提出一系列更精细的问题，从而精确定位任何单个比特错误的位置。

cues.en: The overall feeling is a bit like playing a game of 20 questions, asking yes or no queries that chop the space of possibilities in half.
cues.zh: 整体感觉有点像在玩20个问题的游戏，提出是或否的询问，把可能性空间一分为二。

cues.en: For example, let's say we do a parity check just on these eight bits, all of the odd numbered positions.
cues.zh: 例如，假设我们只对这八个比特做奇偶校验，也就是所有奇数位置。

cues.en: Then if an error is detected, it gives the receiver a little more information about where specifically the error is, namely that it's in an odd position.
cues.zh: 那么如果检测到错误，它就给接收方提供了更多关于错误具体位置的信息，即错误在奇数位置。

cues.en: If no error is detected among those eight bits, it either means there's no error at all, or it sits somewhere in the even positions.
cues.zh: 如果这八个比特中没有检测到错误，要么意味着根本没有错误，要么错误位于偶数位置。

cues.en: You might think that limiting a parity check to half the bits makes it less effective. But when it's done in conjunction with other well chosen checks, it counterintuitively gives us something a lot more powerful.
cues.zh: 你可能会认为，把奇偶校验限制在一半的比特上会降低它的效果。但当它与其他精心选择的校验结合使用时，反直觉地给了我们更强大的东西。

cues.en: To actually set up that parity check, remember, it requires earmarking some special bit that has control for the parity of that full group.
cues.zh: 要真正建立这个奇偶校验，记住，需要专门预留一个特殊的位，用来控制整组的奇偶性。

cues.en: Here, let's just choose position number one. So for the example shown, the parity of these eight bits is currently odd, so the sender is responsible for toggling that parity bit, and now it's even.
cues.zh: 这里我们就选第1个位置。所以在所示例子中，这八个位的奇偶性目前是奇数，因此发送方要负责翻转那个校验位，现在它就变成偶数了。

cues.en: This is only one out of four parity checks that we'll do. The second check is gonna be among the eight bits on the right half of the grid, at least as we've drawn it here. This time we might use position number two as a parity bit.
cues.zh: 这只是我们要做的四项奇偶校验之一。第二项校验将针对网格右半边的八个位，至少按我们这里的画法是这样。这次我们可能用第2个位置作为校验位。

cues.en: So these eight bits already have an even parity, and the sender can feel good leaving that bit number two unchanged.
cues.zh: 所以这八个位已经是偶校验，发送方可以安心让第2位保持不变。

cues.en: Then on the other end, if the receiver checks the parity of this group and they find that it's odd, they'll know that the error is somewhere among these eight bits on the right. Otherwise, it means either there's no error or the error is somewhere on the left half.
cues.zh: 然后在接收端，如果接收方检查这一组的奇偶性，发现是奇数，就会知道错误在右边这八个位中的某处。否则，就意味着要么没有错误，要么错误在左半边某处。

cues.en: Or I guess there could have been two errors, but for right now, we're gonna assume that there's at most one error in the entire block. Things break down completely for more than that. Here, before we look at the next two checks, take a moment to think about what these first two allow us to do when you consider them together.
cues.zh: 或者我想也可能出现了两个错误，但现在我们假设整个块中最多只有一个错误。超过一个就完全失效了。这里，在看接下来两项校验之前，先花点时间想想：把前两项放在一起看，它们能让我们做什么。

cues.en: Let's say you detect an error among the odd columns and among the right half. It necessarily means the error is somewhere in the last column.
cues.zh: 假设你在奇数列中检测到错误，同时又在右半边检测到错误。那必然意味着错误在最后一列的某处。

cues.en: If there was no error in the odd column, but there was one in the right half, well, that tells you it's in the second to last column.
cues.zh: 如果奇数位那一列没有错误，但右半部分有错，那就说明错误在倒数第二列。

cues.en: Likewise, if there is an error in the odd columns, not in the right half, you know that it's somewhere in the second column. And then if neither of those two parity checks detects anything, it means the only place that an error could be is in that leftmost column.
cues.zh: 同样，如果奇数位列有错，而右半部分没有错，那你就知道错误在第二列的某个位置。如果这两项奇偶校验都没有检测到任何问题，那就意味着唯一可能出错的地方就是最左边那一列。

cues.en: But it also might simply mean there's no error at all, which is all a rather belabored way to say that two parity checks let us pin down the column.
cues.zh: 但这也可能只是说明根本没有错误。啰嗦了半天，其实就是说两项奇偶校验让我们能确定出错的是哪一列。

cues.en: From here, you can probably guess what follows. We do basically the same thing, for the rows. There's gonna be a parity check on the odd rows using position four as a parity bit. So in this example, that group already has an even parity, so bit four would be set to a zero.
cues.zh: 到这里，你大概能猜到接下来是什么了。我们对行做基本相同的操作。用第四位作为校验位，对奇数行进行奇偶校验。在这个例子中，那一组已经是偶校验了，所以第四位会被设为 0。

cues.en: And finally, there's a parity check on the bottom two rows using position eight as a parity bit. In this case, it looks like the sender needs to turn that bit eight on in order to give the group even parity.
cues.zh: 最后，用第八位作为校验位，对最下面两行进行奇偶校验。在这个例子中，发送方似乎需要把第八位打开，才能让这一组变成偶校验。

cues.en: Just as the first two checks let us pin down the column, these next two let you pin down the row.
cues.zh: 就像前两项校验让我们确定了列，接下来这两项让你确定了行。

cues.en: As an example, imagine that during the transmission, there's an error at, say, position three.
cues.zh: 举个例子，假设在传输过程中，比如说第三位出了错。

cues.en: Well, this affects the first parity group, and it also affects the second parity group. So the receiver knows that there's an error somewhere in that right column,
cues.zh: 这会影响第一个奇偶校验组，也会影响第二个奇偶校验组。所以接收方就知道右边那一列的某个地方出了错，

cues.en: but it doesn't affect the third group,
cues.zh: 但它不影响第三组，

cues.en: and it doesn't affect the fourth group.
cues.zh: 也不影响第四组。

cues.en: And that lets the receiver pinpoint the error up to the first row, which necessarily means position three, so they can fix the error.
cues.zh: 这样接收方就能把错误定位到第一行，也就必然是第三位，从而修正错误。

cues.en: You might enjoy taking a moment to convince yourself that the answers to these four questions really will always let you pin down a specific location no matter where they turn out to be.
cues.zh: 你可以花点时间说服自己，这四个问题的答案确实总能让你锁定具体位置，无论错误出现在哪里。

cues.en: In fact, the astute among you might even notice a connection between these questions and binary counting. And if you do, again, let me emphasize, pause. Try for yourself to draw the connection before I spoil it.
cues.zh: 事实上，敏锐的人可能已经注意到这些问题和二进制计数之间的联系。如果你发现了，我再强调一次，暂停。在我揭晓之前，自己试着画出这个联系。

cues.en: If you're wondering what happens if a parity bit itself gets affected,
cues.zh: 如果你想知道校验位本身出问题会怎样，

cues.en: well, you can just try it. Take a moment to think about how any error among these four special bits is gonna be tracked down just like any other with the same group of four questions.
cues.zh: 那你可以试试看。花点时间想一想，这四个特殊位中的任何错误，都会像其他错误一样，用同样的四个问题被追踪定位。

cues.en: It doesn't really matter since at the end of the day, what we want is to protect the message bits. The error correction bits are just riding along. But protecting those bits as well is something that naturally falls out of the scheme as a byproduct.
cues.zh: 这其实不太重要，因为归根结底，我们要保护的是消息位。纠错位只是顺带搭车。但保护这些位本身，也会作为副产品自然地从这套方案中得出。

cues.en: You might also enjoy anticipating how this scales.
cues.zh: 你可能也会乐于预想它如何扩展。

cues.en: If we used a block of size 256
cues.zh: 比如，如果我们用大小为 256

cues.en: bits, for example, order to pin down a location, you need only eight yes or no questions to binary search your way down to some specific spot.
cues.zh: 位的块，要锁定一个位置，只需要八个是或否的问题，就能用二分查找定位到某个具体位置。

cues.en: And remember, each question requires giving up only a single bit to set the appropriate parity check.
cues.zh: 记住，每个问题只需让出一个位来设置相应的校验。

cues.en: Some of you may already see it, but we'll talk later about the systematic way to find what these questions are in just a minute or two. Hopefully, this sketch is enough to appreciate the efficiency of what we're developing here. Everything, except for those eight highlighted parity bits, can be whatever you want it to be, carrying whatever message or data you want.
cues.zh: 有些人可能已经看出来了，但稍后我们会用一两分钟讲讲系统性找出这些问题的办法。希望这张草图足以让你体会到我们正在开发的东西有多高效。除了那八个高亮的校验位之外，其他所有位都可以随你设定，承载你想要的任何消息或数据。

cues.en: The eight bits are redundant in the sense that they're completely determined by the rest of the message, but it's in a much smarter way than simply copying the message as a whole.
cues.zh: 这八个比特是冗余的，因为它们完全由消息的其余部分决定，但方式比简单地把整条消息复制一遍要聪明得多。

cues.en: And still, for so little given up, you would be able to identify and fix any single bit error.
cues.zh: 而且，付出这么小的代价，你就能识别并修复任意单个比特错误。

cues.en: Well, almost. Okay. So the one problem here is that if none of the four parity checks detect an error, meaning that the specially selected subsets of eight bits all have even parities just like the sender intended,
cues.zh: 嗯，差不多吧。好吧。这里的一个问题是，如果四个校验都没有检测到错误，也就是说，特别选定的那八个比特子集全都具有和发送方预期一样的偶校验，

cues.en: then it either means there was no error at all, or it narrows us down into position zero.
cues.zh: 那么要么意味着根本没有错误，要么就把我们缩小到了第零个位置。

cues.en: You see, with four yes or no questions, we have 16 possible outcomes for our parity checks. And at first, that feels perfect for pinpointing one out of 16 positions in the block. But you also need to communicate a seventeenth outcome, the no error condition.
cues.zh: 你看，用四个是或否的问题，我们的校验就有16种可能的结果。乍一看，这刚好适合从块中16个位置里 pinpoint 出一个。但你还需要传达第十七种结果，即无错误状态。

cues.en: The solution here is actually pretty simple. Just forget about that zeroth bit entirely.
cues.zh: 这里的解决办法其实很简单。干脆完全忘掉那个第零位。

cues.en: So when we do our four parity checks and we see that they're all even, it unambiguously
cues.zh: 所以当我们做四个校验，发现它们全都是偶校验时，就明确无误地

cues.en: means that there is no error.
cues.zh: 意味着没有错误。

cues.en: What that means is rather than working with a 16 bit block, we work with a 15 bit block, where 11 of the bits are free to carry a message and four of them are there for redundancy.
cues.zh: 也就是说，我们不再处理 16 位块，而是处理 15 位块，其中 11 位可以自由携带消息，另外 4 位用于冗余。

cues.en: And with that, we now have what people in the business would refer to as a fifteen eleven Hamming code.
cues.zh: 这样一来，我们就得到了业内所说的十五十一汉明码。

cues.en: That said, it is nice to have a block size that's a clean power of two, and there's a clever way that we can keep that zeroth bit around and get it to do a little extra work for us.
cues.zh: 话虽如此，块大小是干净的 2 的幂确实不错，而且有一种巧妙的方法可以保留那个第零位，让它为我们多做一点工作。

cues.en: If we use it as a parity bit across the whole block, it lets us actually detect, even though we can't correct, two bit errors.
cues.zh: 如果我们把它用作整个块的奇偶校验位，它就能让我们实际检测到两位错误，尽管无法纠正。

cues.en: Here's how it works. After setting those four special error correcting bits, we set that zero th one so that the parity of the full block is even, just like a normal parity check.
cues.zh: 原理是这样的。设置好那四个特殊的纠错位后，我们再设置第零位，使整个块的奇偶性为偶，就像普通的奇偶校验一样。

cues.en: Now if there's a single bit error, then the parity of the full block toggles to be odd, but we would catch that anyway, thanks to the four error correcting checks.
cues.zh: 现在如果出现单比特错误，整个块的奇偶性就会翻转为奇，但多亏了那四个纠错校验，我们本来就能捕捉到它。

cues.en: However, if there's two errors, then the overall parity is gonna toggle back to being even, But the receiver would still see that there's been at least some error because of what's going on with those four usual parity checks.
cues.zh: 然而，如果出现两个错误，总体奇偶性会翻回偶，但接收方仍会看到至少存在某种错误，因为那四个常规奇偶校验的情况不对劲。

cues.en: So if they notice an even parity overall,
cues.zh: 所以如果他们注意到总体是偶校验，

cues.en: but something non zero happening with the other checks, it tells them there were at least two errors.
cues.zh: 但其他校验出现了非零的情况，这就告诉他们至少有两个错误。

cues.en: Isn't that clever? Even though we can't correct those two bit errors, just by putting that one little bothersome zeroth bit back to work, it lets us detect them.
cues.zh: 是不是很巧妙？虽然我们无法纠正那两位错误，但只要把那个烦人的第零位重新利用起来，就能检测出它们。

cues.en: This is pretty standard. It's known as an extended Hamming code.
cues.zh: 这是很标准的做法，叫做扩展汉明码。

cues.en: Technically speaking, you now have a full description of what a Hamming code does, at least for the example of a 16 bit block.
cues.zh: 严格来说，你现在已经完整了解了汉明码的作用，至少对于16位块的例子是这样。

cues.en: But I think you'll find it more satisfying to check your understanding and solidify everything up to this point by doing one full example from start to finish yourself.
cues.zh: 但我觉得，自己从头到尾完整做一遍例子来检验理解、巩固之前的内容，会让你更有成就感。

cues.en: I'll step through it with you though, so you can check yourself.
cues.zh: 不过我会陪你一步步过，方便你对照检查。

cues.en: To set up a message, whether that's a literal message that you're translating over space or some data that you wanna store over time,
cues.zh: 要设置一条消息，不管是跨空间传输的字面消息，还是想随时间存储的数据，

cues.en: the first step is to divide it up into 11 bit chunks.
cues.zh: 第一步是把它分成11位的块。

cues.en: Each chunk is gonna get packaged into an error resistant 16 bit block. So let's take this one as an example and actually work it out. Go ahead. Actually do it. Pause and try putting together this block.
cues.zh: 每一块都会被打包成一个抗错的16位块。那我们拿这个作为例子，实际算一遍。来吧，真的动手做。暂停一下，试着拼出这个块。

cues.en: Okay. You ready? Remember, position zero along with the other powers of two are reserved for error correction duty. So you start by placing the message bits in all of the remaining spots in order.
cues.zh: 好，准备好了吗？记住，第零位和其他2的幂次位置都保留给纠错用。所以先把消息位按顺序放进剩下所有位置。

cues.en: You need this group to have an even parity, which it already does, so you should have set that parity bit in position one to be a zero.
cues.zh: 你需要这一组具有偶校验，而它已经是偶校验了，所以位置1的校验位应该设为0。

cues.en: The next group starts off with an odd parity, so you should have set its parity bit to be one.
cues.zh: 下一组以奇校验开头，所以你应该把它的校验位设为一。

cues.en: The group after that starts with an odd parity, so again, you should have set its parity bit to one. And the final group also has an odd parity, meaning we set that bit in position eight to be a one.
cues.zh: 再下一组也以奇校验开头，所以同样应该把它的校验位设为一。最后一组也是奇校验，意味着我们要把第八位的校验位设为一。

cues.en: And then as the final step, the full block now has an even parity,
cues.zh: 然后作为最后一步，整个数据块现在是偶校验，

cues.en: meaning that you can set that bit number zero, the overarching parity bit, to be zero.
cues.zh: 这意味着你可以把第零位，也就是总校验位，设为零。

cues.en: So as this block is sent off, the parity of the four special subsets and the block as a whole will all be even or zero.
cues.zh: 所以当这个数据块发送出去时，四个特殊子集和整个数据块的校验都会是偶数或零。

cues.en: As the second part of the exercise, let's have you play the role of the receiver.
cues.zh: 作为练习的第二部分，让你来扮演接收方的角色。

cues.en: Of course, that would mean you don't already know what this message is. Maybe some of you memorized it, but let's assume that you haven't.
cues.zh: 当然，这意味着你事先并不知道这条消息是什么。也许有人已经记住了，但我们假设你没有。

cues.en: What I'm gonna do is change either zero, one, or two of the bits in that block, and then ask you to figure out what it is that I did.
cues.zh: 我要做的是改动那个数据块中零个、一个或两个位，然后让你来判断我改了什么。

cues.en: So again, pause and try working it out.
cues.zh: 所以再次暂停，试着解出来。

cues.en: Okay. So you as the receiver, now check the first parity group, and you can see that it's even. So any error that exists would have to be in an even column.
cues.zh: 好。现在你作为接收方，检查第一个校验组，可以看到它是偶数。所以任何存在的错误都必然在偶数列中。

cues.en: The next check gives us an odd number, telling us both that there's at least one error and narrowing us down into this specific column.
cues.zh: 下一次检查给出奇数，这既告诉我们至少有一个错误，也把范围缩小到了这一特定的列。

cues.en: The third check is even, chopping down the possibilities even further.
cues.zh: 第三次检查是偶数，进一步缩小了可能性。

cues.en: And the last parity check is odd, telling us there's an error somewhere in the bottom, which by now we can see must be in position number 10.
cues.zh: 最后一个奇偶校验位是奇数，说明底部某处有错误，现在我们已经能看出必定在第10位。

cues.en: What's more, the parity of the whole block is odd, giving us confidence that there was one flip and not two. If it's three or more, all bets are off.
cues.zh: 而且，整个块的奇偶校验结果是奇数，这让我们确信只发生了一次翻转，而不是两次。如果是三次或更多，那就无法确定了。

cues.en: After correcting that bit number 10, pulling out the 11 bits that were not used for correction gives us the relevant segment of the original message,
cues.zh: 纠正第10位之后，取出那11个未用于纠错的比特，就得到了原始消息的相关片段，

cues.en: which if you rewind and compare, is indeed exactly what we started the example with.
cues.zh: 如果你回退对比，确实正是我们开始这个示例时的内容。

cues.en: And now that you know how to do all this by hand, I'd like to show you how you can carry out the core part of all of this logic with a single line of Python code.
cues.zh: 现在你已经知道如何手工完成这一切，我想展示给你看，如何用一行Python代码实现这整套逻辑的核心部分。

cues.en: You see, what I haven't told you yet is just how elegant this algorithm really is, how simple it is to get a machine to point to the position of an error, how to systematically scale it, and how we can frame all of this as one single operation rather than multiple separate parity checks.
cues.zh: 你看，我还没告诉你的是，这个算法究竟有多优雅，让机器指出错误位置有多简单，如何系统性地扩展它，以及我们如何能把这一切构建为单一操作，而不是多次独立的奇偶校验。
